metadata.purpose: Reduce data-loss and endpoint-compromise risk by allowing the sensitive lab application only from a device that reports compliant state.
metadata.scope: Shared lab users and lab administrators accessing the single SENSITIVE_APP_ID resource from Windows, across all client app types.
metadata.exclusions: The shared emergency-access group and a named, time-bounded device exception group.
metadata.controls: Require the device to be marked compliant. CA001 or CA002 independently supplies the applicable authentication requirement.
prerequisites: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or qualifying suite licences for in-scope users
Microsoft Intune licences and an assigned compliance policy
Test device is registered in Microsoft Entra ID, enrolled in Intune, and has reported compliance
Supported operating system and browser/client capable of presenting device identity
Sensitive enterprise application ID is verified in the target tenant
metadata.expectedUserImpact: For the sensitive app on Windows, a recognized compliant device satisfies this policy; an unmanaged, unknown, or noncompliant device would fail the grant control when enforced. The Windows-only pilot avoids known report-only device-certificate prompts on macOS, iOS, and Android. Until Intune prerequisites and tenant evidence exist, this scenario remains designed but unverified.
metadata.owner: Zero Trust Identity & Conditional Access Lab
